_why_this_file_is_here: A TEST fixture, not a default. The server ships with NO page description on purpose: a default inside the package would be one tenant's copy compiled back into the generic package, and a second tenant would still cost a code change. Tests need a tenant to be, so they bring their own. The values below are deliberately NOT the live site's, so a test cannot pass by accidentally reading production copy.
_chrome_note: chrome_css_file is added by the test at runtime, as an absolute path to chrome-for-tests.css, because writing an absolute path into a checked-in fixture is the exact defect T2 removed from the server and would be hypocritical here. No chrome_css_export is set ON PURPOSE: the live set's chrome is a module exporting a template literal, this one is a plain .css file that IS the css, so between them both branches of chromeCssFor run and neither is a file-extension guess.
_one_entry: One entry, so it serves whatever host the test configures and needs no `hosts` key. The two-tenant test writes its own file with two entries that DO declare hosts.
